relevance_note: The paper describes four individual patients with TNFAIP3 variants: 'WES revealed heterozygous c.559C > T in the TNFAIP3 gene in P1, P2 and P3'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON from values I chose and resolved spaces in spans to the paper's exact characters (the paper uses thin spaces, e.g. in 'c.559C > T'); every span was then checked verbatim. Labels: the text calls the patients P1-P4 (Table 1/2 use bare numbers 1-4, Table 3 'Case 1/2/4'), so rule 1 gives P1-P4; Table 3 'Case n' columns were read as Pn. P4's parents (tested negative: 'the mutation was not found in her parents') get rows 'parent of P4' and 'parent of P4 2'. Other members of family 1 (WES 'included all members in Fig. 1'; 'the mutation was not detected in other members in family 1'; Fig. 3 legend lists F, M, GF, GM) are not described individually, so no rows; the mother of P1/P2 and the grandparents are not individually described in the text. Table 2 columns (No, Fever, Ulcers, Musculoskeletal, Cardiovascular, Intestinal, Thyroid, Liver, lung, Genotype, Mutation origin): the word 'No' was read as an explicit absence (not an undefined symbol). The 'Ulcers' column (values 'No'/'Oral') was read as mucocutaneous (oral/genital) ulcers, separate from the 'Intestinal' column, so 'No' there was not used against P2's endoscopic GI ulcers. Broad 'No' cells were used to exclude narrower checklist items (Musculoskeletal No -> arthritis/arthralgia; Intestinal No -> GI ulcers/inflammation; Thyroid No -> autoimmune thyroiditis; Liver No -> autoimmune hepatitis; lung No -> ILD; Fever No -> recurrent fever); 'Cardiovascular No' was not used for 'pericarditis or other serositis' or vasculitis (composite items). Table 3 is patients-as-columns with a two-row header (Case 1, Case 1, Case 2, Case 2, Case 4, Case 4 / Pretherapy, posttherapy, ...); only pretherapy ESR and CRP (P2, P4) and anti-dsDNA (P1) were used; 'elevated' was read from values above the printed normal range; '-' in Table 3 is not defined as negative, so not used. No stacked ' / ' cells. Uveitis/eye and skin items are excluded for all four patients from the named group statement 'All patients had no signs of eye or skin problems' (evidence basis: inferred from group statement). Contradictions in the paper: (1) P2 onset 'at age 2.6' in text vs '2.5 years' in Table 1 (table value recorded for age at onset); (2) P4 '9-year-old' and onset 'at the age of 7 years' in text vs current age 8.3 years and onset 6.9 years in Table 1 (table values recorded); (3) P4 oral ulcers in text vs Table 2 Ulcers 'No' (both rows emitted; checklist oral ulcers not reported); (4) P4 'positive ANA and anti-ds DNA antibodies' at referral vs 'no other autoantibody was detected' and Table 3 anti-dsDNA '–' (both rows emitted); (5) P1 'other autoantibodies were negative' vs Table 3 anti-dsDNA '+' for Case 1 pretherapy (both rows emitted); (6) Fig. 2 legend attributes knee synovitis (2e) and ILD (2f) to P3, while the text cites Fig. 2e and 2f for P4 and Table 2 gives P3 lung 'No' (legend rows emitted for P3; P3 ILD checklist not reported); (7) P4 Table 1 current treatment lists CSA and diclofenac sodium, text lists only etanercept with low dose prednisolone. Inheritance: P1 and P2 'inherited paternal' (Table 2 origin 'Father'; father P3 carries the variant). P3 left 'not reported' although the authors call it de novo, because testing of P3's own parents is not stated explicitly (rule 8); the authors' statement is quoted in parental_testing_statement. P4 'de novo' (variant not found in her parents). Variant type 'nonsense' only for p.R87X (stated); not stated for p.Q187X. Pathogenicity left 'not reported' (the paper calls c.259C > T 'novel' and says c.559C > T was reported by another study [16], neither is a classification). Hypothyroidism (P1) was not taken as autoimmune thyroiditis; pericardial effusion and ascites (P1) were not taken as serositis; P3's anal fistula (archosyrinx) was not taken as GI ulcers/inflammation. P1 cytopenia (autoimmune) marked observed from leukopenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia with a positive Coombs test. Vital status left not reported (not stated). P4 'no family history of rheumatic diseases' was not turned into features for her parents.
